title: Writing the Project Documents: Requirement, Feature, Function, UML
summary: Using the study logger as the example, learn how the four documents (requirements REQ, features FEAT, function contracts FUNC and UML) describe one program from different angles. Run a skeleton that has only contracts and a version with F1 implemented, and carry out each requirement's check yourself at the keyboard.

study_logger_skeleton.summary: A skeleton that turns the Week 10 design document into code. Every function has a name, parameters and a docstring (the contract), but its body is raise NotImplementedError or a TODO placeholder. See how the document's function table (FUNC) became files and functions as it is.
steps: There are four modules, main.py, logic.py, storage.py and report.py, plus data/study.csv. The CSV holds the header date,course,minutes and two rows: python 90 minutes and stats 45 minutes.

This prints Loaded 0 records and TODO: totals. It says 0 even though the file has two rows because load_records() is still a placeholder that returns an empty list. It runs, but it does not yet satisfy the requirements (REQ-03, REQ-04).

The contract written in the function document (DOC 3) is there as the docstring. Read the shape of the return value {"date", "course", "minutes": int}, the lower-casing, and the conditions that raise ValueError.

All six functions from the function table (parse_minutes, make_record, weekly_totals, load_records, append_record, format_totals) and main() are present, and each body is marked with NotImplementedError or TODO. Every function name is a verb plus a noun.

Calling a function that has no body yet gives a NotImplementedError: parse_minutes traceback. At the skeleton stage this is normal. From the next session on, these lines are replaced one by one with real bodies.

study_logger_f1.summary: A version in which FEAT-01 "Log one entry" works end to end. main() asks for the date, course and minutes, logic.make_record() checks them, and storage.append_record() appends one row to data/study.csv. Type in the requirement document's checks REQ-01 and REQ-02 exactly as written.
steps: This file turns the requirements' checks into asserts. All checks passed. appears only if parse_minutes("90") is 90, " Python " is cleaned up to python, and an empty course, -30 and abc are all rejected.

The make_record() example from the slide. It prints python 90. The course has its leading and trailing spaces removed and is lower-cased, and minutes is the integer 90, not the string "90" (repr shows no quotes).

The check for REQ-01: entering 2026-11-10, python, 90 prints Saved. and adds one new row, 2026-11-10,python,90, at the end of study.csv. The three prompts appear run together on one line because the input was piped in.
The check for REQ-02: -30 minutes is rejected with Not saved: minutes must be positive, got -30, and the line counts before and after are the same. The file being unchanged is the observable result.

The error lines of the feature sheet (FEAT-01): a course made only of spaces gives course must not be empty, and non-numeric minutes give int()'s ValueError message, both as Not saved. In both cases main() catches the ValueError and writes nothing.

The F1 path (make_record, parse_minutes, append_record) has no TODOs. load_records() (F2) and weekly_totals() and format_totals() (F3) are still left, so REQ-03 weekly totals and REQ-04 keeping records between runs cannot be checked with this version.
